title: Law of the First Fountain
text: A damaged traveler journal records: Citizens could petition the crown by placing a silver shell in the eastern palace fountain.

title: Banner Order
text: An old field report states: Royal banners displayed civic duties by knot pattern, allowing decrees to be read through dark water.

title: The Empty Coronation
text: A local record preserves this account: A court record describes a crown placed on an empty throne while every noble swore loyalty anyway.

title: Sealkeeper's Oath
text: An unsigned observation reads: Breaking a royal seal required three witnesses, a tide-priest, and a written apology to the door.

title: Portrait Improvement
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki wrote: "The king looked too serious, so I supplied the traditional mustache. Tradition began today."

title: Foreign Compact
text: An old field report states: An embassy ledger records the arrival of researchers offering preservation methods in exchange for royal protection.

title: Drowned Market Law
text: A local record preserves this account: Merchants were forbidden to sell memories, shadows, or weather captured outside the kingdom.

title: The Queen's Measure
text: An unsigned observation reads: Public fountains were calibrated against the queen's chalice and still fill to precisely the same depth.

title: Court of Echoes
text: A damaged traveler journal records: Petitioners spoke through carved masks so the throne judged arguments without recognizing rank.

title: Unhelpful Palace Map
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki labeled every stairway "up-ish" and every sealed treasury "probably snacks."

title: The Tax on Pearls
text: A local record preserves this account: Pearls formed inside royal waters belonged one-third to the finder, one-third to the crown, and one-third to the sea.

title: Treaty Chamber Draft
text: An unsigned observation reads: The organization promised defensive constructs while reserving unrestricted access to royal ruins and prisoners.

title: The Crownless Guard
text: A damaged traveler journal records: After the palace fell, surviving guards removed their crests but continued patrolling the evacuation routes.

title: Banquet Protocol
text: An old field report states: Guests received seven utensils, three of which were ceremonial and one of which was reportedly alive.

title: Returned Embassy Key
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki's annotation reads: "Borrowed during an emergency. Returned during a different century. Still counts."

title: Royal Archive Flooding
text: An unsigned observation reads: Archivists deliberately flooded the lowest stacks to hide politically dangerous records in salt-preserved cases.

title: The Prince Without a Name
text: A damaged traveler journal records: One nursery ledger removes an heir from every succession list without explaining whether he died or was erased.

title: Covenant Engine Clause
text: An old field report states: A treaty permits royal seals to command facility constructs, but only while the ancient bloodline endures.

title: Law Beneath the Law
text: A local record preserves this account: An older tablet states that no crown may own a living mind, contradicting several later royal decrees.

title: Officer Portrait Gallery
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki added paper crowns to the Officers and a note: "Now everyone is equally overqualified."

title: The Menagerie Petition
text: A damaged traveler journal records: Keepers begged the court to release creatures altered by visiting researchers; the petition was denied.

title: Council Vote
text: An old field report states: Three ministers opposed the Compact, two vanished, and the surviving record lists the decision as unanimous.

title: Seal Number Seven
text: A local record preserves this account: The seventh seal bears both royal script and the same Subject Seven notation used in facility records.

title: The Last Public Notice
text: An unsigned observation reads: Citizens were ordered away from the palace while research personnel received protected passage inward.

title: Throne Room Correction
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki scratched out "eternal authority" and wrote "very temporary furniture."

title: The Drowned Constitution
text: An old field report states: Fragments preserve rights to safe currents, honest measures, and freedom from magical alteration.

title: Compact Renewal
text: A local record preserves this account: Successor rulers renewed the organization's privileges long after the original signatories should have died.

title: The Royal Price
text: An unsigned observation reads: A private letter suggests the crown exchanged political prisoners for defenses against an approaching Astral threat.

title: Embassy Closure
text: A damaged traveler journal records: The final embassy log seals its staff inside under Continuance orders rather than royal command.

title: No Throne Is Forever
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: An unknown clerk wrote that kingdoms drown, institutions change names, and records remember both.
